areas.name: New-hire ramp
areas.q: New reps follow a written plan for their first 30 days instead of shadowing whoever is free.
areas.fix: Write a one-page 30-day plan: one skill per week, who trains it, and what a new rep must show you by Friday.

areas.name: Practice
areas.q: Reps roleplay real customer conversations at least once a week.
areas.fix: Run one 10-minute roleplay every week on the objection you heard most. Pair reps up, swap roles, and give one note each.

areas.name: Objection handling
areas.q: Every rep answers the five most common objections the same, proven way.
areas.fix: Agree on one answer for each of your top five objections and put it on a card every rep carries.

areas.name: Follow-up
areas.q: Every customer who leaves without buying gets a follow-up plan within 24 hours.
areas.fix: Make an end-of-day rule: no unsold customer goes home without a next contact date in the CRM, checked by a manager.

areas.name: Knowing the numbers
areas.q: Each rep can tell you their own closing ratio, appointments and units for the month.
areas.fix: Have every rep track three numbers daily (conversations, appointments, sales) and review them with you on Friday.

areas.name: One-on-one coaching
areas.q: Every rep gets a one-on-one coaching conversation with a manager every week.
areas.fix: Block 15 minutes per rep per week. Ask three questions: what went well, what got stuck, what one thing you'll do differently.

areas.name: Recognition
areas.q: Top performers are recognized in front of the team every month with something they can keep.
areas.fix: Name a Closer of the Month at your first meeting of the month, say exactly what they did, and hand them something they keep.
areas.linkText: See Closer of the Month awards

areas.name: Morning huddle
areas.q: The team starts each day with a short, focused huddle that trains one skill.
areas.fix: Keep huddles to 10 minutes: one number, one skill drilled for two minutes, one goal per rep for the day.

areas.name: Keeping reps
areas.q: Most new reps are still on the team after 90 days.
areas.fix: Check in with every new rep at day 30, 60 and 90. Ask what would make them quit, and fix the first thing they name.

areas.name: Bouncing back
areas.q: After a slow week, the team gets back to work instead of complaining or coasting.
areas.fix: After a slow week, name it in Monday's huddle, pick one activity number to win this week, and celebrate the first rep who hits it.
areas.linkText: Have reps take the Unbroken Assessment

tiers.label: Field Ready
tiers.text: Your team has strong habits. The opportunity is keeping them sharp and recognizing the people carrying the store.

tiers.label: Solid Base, Leaking Deals
tiers.text: The foundation is there, but a few gaps are costing you deals and reps every month. Fix your lowest three and the rest gets easier.

tiers.label: At Risk
tiers.text: Your reps are mostly figuring it out alone. Expect turnover and missed deals until practice, follow-up and coaching become routine.

tiers.label: Rebuild the Routine
tiers.text: Right now the team runs on talent and luck. A simple weekly rhythm of practice, numbers and recognition will change things fast.
